title: Quantum Frozen--Oseen homotopy analysis method with LCHS for solving nonlinear partial differential equations
authors: Jinhao Yuan, Leyu Chen, Tiegang Liu, Kun Wang
abstract: Nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) underpin computational fluid dynamics, yet resolving nonlinear transport on fine grids remains computationally demanding. Quantum linear-evolution algorithms offer a possible route to large-scale simulation but cannot directly propagate nonlinear coupling. Here we develop a Frozen--Oseen quantum homotopy method (FOQHAM) framework that links transport-aware auxiliary-operator selection to the size of the resulting linear representation. We freeze the full Fréchet derivative at a prescribed flow profile, retaining transport and profile-gradient coupling and close each prescribed finite-order homotopy hierarchy as a fixed affine linear system by product lifting. We formulate its propagation through Linear Combinations of Hamiltonian Simulations (LCHS), without outer homotopy iterations or profile updates. For spatially semidiscrete equations, we establish local approximation bounds and exact closure of the finite-order hierarchy. Classical tests on Burgers, Korteweg--de Vries, Zakharov--Kuznetsov, and one- and two-dimensional isothermal compressible Navier--Stokes equations provide numerical evidence of accurate non-iterative approximations in the tested regimes. The framework thus connects nonlinear PDE approximation to quantum linear evolution and offers a conditional path toward quantum acceleration.
summary: This paper presents the Quantum Frozen-Oseen Homotopy Analysis Method (FOQHAM) to tackle the computational difficulty of nonlinear PDEs. It achieves this by linking the nonlinear problem to a linear evolution framework using LCHS, allowing for non-iterative approximations. The method is demonstrated on classical fluid dynamics models, offering a conditional path toward quantum acceleration for such simulations.
main_problem: The paper addresses the computational challenge of solving nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs), particularly in fluid dynamics, where nonlinear transport on fine grids is demanding.
main_result: The developed framework successfully links nonlinear PDE approximation to quantum linear evolution, providing a non-iterative approximation path for classical tests like the Navier-Stokes equations.
method: It introduces the Quantum Frozen-Oseen Homotopy Analysis Method (FOQHAM), which uses a frozen Fréchet derivative and propagates the resulting linear system via Linear Combinations of Hamiltonian Simulations (LCHS).
model_or_system: The method is applied to general nonlinear PDEs, including the Burgers, Korteweg-de Vries (KdV), Zakharov-Kuznetsov, and isothermal compressible Navier-Stokes equations.
key_observables: Local approximation bounds, contraction factors ($\alpha_{	ext{HAM}}$), and the convergence of the deformation series ($\Phi(q)$).
important_parameters: The homotopy parameter $q \in [0, 1]$, the auxiliary-operator selection, and the contraction factor $\alpha_{	ext{HAM}} < 1$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes local regularity bounds on the Fréchet derivative and requires the frozen operator to generate a strongly continuous semigroup.
paper_structure: The paper develops the FOQHAM framework by first defining the frozen-Oseen decomposition, then formulating the problem via a homotopy deformation series, and finally showing how LCHS propagates the resulting linear system, concluding with classical PDE tests.
why_interesting: While the core application is classical PDE solving, the explicit integration of quantum linear evolution (LCHS) to approximate nonlinear dynamics makes it highly relevant to quantum simulation techniques for open quantum systems.

Colored curves are finite-K1/K2 Frozen–Oseen HAM-LCHS results at the indicated orders; the µ row also shows a first-order endpoint-profile result.
